title: Align the shelf-label units
hook: €0.80 per 100g or €7 per kg: which label is lower?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert prices quoted per 100g and per kilogram to a common unit.

misconception: The smaller number on a price label is always cheaper.
objective: Convert prices quoted per 100g and per kilogram to a common unit.

claims.text: A is €0.80 per 100g. B is €7 per kg. Scaled model; fictional prices; 1kg=1000g.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Price per kg=7€, A=8€/kg and B=7€/kg. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A kilogram contains ten 100g units. Multiply the 100g price by ten before comparing. A smaller printed price can describe a smaller amount rather than a cheaper product.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Two fictional shelf labels: €0.65 per 100g and €6 per kg. Which is lower per kilogram? Correct: €6 per kg. A kilogram is ten 100g units, so €0.65 per 100g is €6.50 per kg; the smaller printed number described a smaller amount.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",0.8,10]; B="x"; x denotes Kg-price. At x=7, A=8, B=7. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/recall-patch-resources.lines.txt), applied 2026-10-14 by demo-builder; c4 restates the new recall item. FC LH-4 (2026-10-14, fact-checker, W-380): verified (recall): meta.json recall, resource-specs.json recall and this claim match the patch line; €0.65/100 g = €6.50/kg > €6/kg; option 2 only. Re-computed in node. Record: company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH4-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A unit price is the cost divided by the stated quantity; compare prices only in the same unit.
claims.source: Definition (unit price = cost ÷ stated quantity) and the comparison rule that follows from it: two quotients are comparable only when their denominators are the same unit. The stage's own arithmetic shows it (claims c2-c4). Dataset prices and package amounts are invented for the arithmetic demonstration. Earlier source (labelling practice, now dropped): NIST SP 1181-2025. | Before the 2026-10-15 rewording: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/1181e2025/NIST.SP.1181e2025.html NIST SP 1181-2025, Definitions / Unit Pricing and E-Commerce. Opened 2026-10-13. Dataset prices and package amounts are invented for the arithmetic demonstration. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD UNVERIFIED. Read the engine first. 'A unit price expresses cost per stated quantity' is definitional. But 'comparable unit-price labels use consistent units of measure' is a claim about labelling practice and rests on NIST SP 1181-2025, which I could not open (DNS failure, proxy 403). Left unverified. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. The first half is a definition (cost ÷ quantity). The second half is about labelling practice and rests on NIST SP 1181-2025 (nvlpubs.nist.gov: proxy 403). No source that supports it could be opened from this host: the cited hosts return proxy 403 or fail DNS, and only GitHub raw, PyPI and npm are reachable. I did not verify it from memory or from search snippets.
claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): UNVERIFIED. HELD. NIST SP 1181-2025 (nvlpubs.nist.gov) is not on the allow-list and still returns 403. No allow-listed host carries a unit-pricing standard: OWID has no such page, census.gov redirects to the blocked www host, and PMC has no labelling standard. The first half (unit price = cost ÷ stated quantity) is a definition and holds. The second half, about how comparable labels are made, needs the NIST text. Fix (cm-lifehacks): open NIST SP 1181 from a host that can reach it, or reword to the definition only: 'A unit price is the cost divided by the stated quantity; compare prices only in the same unit.' | Reset to unverified by demo-builder (2026-10-15): W-938 / FC41 rewording applied: definition only; the labelling-practice half (NIST SP 1181, not reachable) is dropped. Not learner-visible as a sentence; the stage divides price by stated quantity. | FC pass 42 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED (definition). Claim is now definition only: unit price = cost ÷ stated quantity, and quotients compare only over the same unit. Checked against the stage (resource-specs.json): A €0.80/100 g × 10 = €8/kg against B €7/kg, so B is lower (key B). Recall €0.65/100 g = €6.50/kg > €6/kg. The labelling-practice half (NIST SP 1181) is dropped. Not a learner sentence.
